correctness.rationale: The explicit XOR graph has 16 vertices, 40 edges, and graph diameter two. Define for each of the 16 candidate landmarks its 780-bit mask of edge pairs separated by min endpoint distance; union recurrence over all 65536 subsets proves no resolved set <=8 and exactly 1600 of size 9. Generate every 9*7 swap of each basis and retain valid basis masks; this yields degree histogram {15:1440,27:160} and 12960 undirected edges. All-source BFS across all 1600 states proves connectivity, 160 eccentricity-six centers and 1440 eccentricity-seven others. Enumerate all 16 translations and 5! direction permutations to get the entire affine action; its orbits have the four stated sizes and distinct omitted-set degree signatures. I performed an independent full Python enumeration from the graph, including all 65536 masks, graph BFS, 1920 affine maps and all-source exchange BFS, agreeing with both repository checker algorithms. Finite exhaustive proof is legitimate because every universe is fully enumerated, unlike partial sample claims.

originality.rationale: Kelenc–Tratnik–Yero introduced edge metric dimension; Milivojević Danas et al. Table 8 explicitly establishes edim(Clebsch)=9. That scalar is not new. The exact labelled count, four symmetry-orbit types, and complete exchange graph radius/diameter are not logical consequences of the quoted scalar and are absent from inspected full 2016 and 2020 papers. Additional unindexed Clebsch reconfiguration or resolving-set census may predate this analysis, so novelty is best-of-knowledge.
residual_risks: An unindexed classification of metric/edge resolving sets or reconfiguration on Clebsch/folded hypercube might reproduce these finite counts.
Results are graph-specific and finite; no extension to arbitrary folded cubes, strongly regular graphs or general exchange graphs is proved.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete minimum-design classification for a standard named strongly regular graph, plus an exact reconfiguration diameter: any optimal edge-identification sensor set can be transformed into any other by at most 7 valid optimum-preserving swaps, and 7 is sharp. The orbit signatures and centers give structural information that the previously known scalar 9 cannot provide. Finite self-contained enumeration is appropriate and exhaustive rather than arbitrary sampled work.

final_claim: The Clebsch graph on F2^4 with difference directions {1,2,4,8,15} has exactly 1600 minimum 9-vertex edge-metric bases (the scalar minimum 9 is previously known), partitioned into affine orbits 160,240,240,960 with four distinct degree signatures on omitted 7-vertex induced subgraphs. Their one-vertex replacement graph has 1600 vertices, 12960 edges, one component, radius 6, diameter 7; the 160 degree-27 bases are its exact centers.
limitations: Exact finite instance only; scalar edim(C)=9 is known and excluded from originality claims.
Classification is for min-endpoint edge distance, labelled bases and one-for-one swaps; no other graph families.
residual_risks: An unindexed classification of metric/edge resolving sets or reconfiguration on Clebsch/folded hypercube might reproduce these finite counts.
Results are graph-specific and finite; no extension to arbitrary folded cubes, strongly regular graphs or general exchange graphs is proved.
